review_type: Independent review of newly surfaced essential source ambiguity and verified Fraud correction
source_gap_verdict: GAP-DEFENSE-OVERSHOOT is genuine and consequential. The reviewed primary text does not uniquely resolve how an indivisible alliance’s excess printed strength is counted in defense. No adequate designer/publisher clarification is present in the supplied evidence.
prior_closure_status: Prior final scoped closure is superseded by this new source-sufficiency finding. Historical passes6/7 remain accurately recorded zero-addition passes, but do not establish current completeness in light of the newly identified outcome branch.

independence.basis: Read supplied new source-only evidence and source-gap claim, then checked the original authoritative pp22/33 independently, read the complete raw eight-post Fraud source thread, and verified actual expanded-v4 bank/key differences. The parent/source researcher’s conclusion was not treated as authoritative.

runtime_model_evidence.log_access: Only permitted turn_context metadata inspected; no session conversation content read.

defense_analysis.case: Only a newly active strength-2 local alliance is available against a strength-1 attack; no other active officers/regiments/alliances.

primary_text.operative_text: Alliance strength can be used for Deploy and defense; the piece is usable once in the purchase turn, and its strength cannot be split among more than one purpose.
Exhaust pieces equal to Crisis strength or as many as possible; if newly exhausted pieces do not equal the Crisis strength, the Crisis succeeds.

defense_analysis.what_is_explicit: The defense uses newly exhausted pieces; matching defense prevents Region Loss. Alliances are eligible defense resources and cannot preserve strength for another purpose after use.
defense_analysis.why_sufficient_strength_is_not_a_derivat: Replacing "equal/do not equal" with ">=/less than" changes the explicit comparison. No reviewed defense passage authorizes that replacement. Saying "the army has enough strength, therefore it wins" assumes the point at issue.
defense_analysis.why_exact_equality_alone_does_not_finish: A literal full-printed-strength accounting would make defense2 not equal attack1 and therefore lose. But the source does not expressly establish that every printed alliance strength point must be counted rather than meeting the single defense with1 and discarding1. The p22 prohibition is on splitting among more than one purpose, not an explicit prohibition on unused excess within a single purpose. Nor does p33 define how "pieces equal to strength" converts a multistrength alliance into contributed defense. Importing full mandatory contribution would be an additional interpretation.
defense_analysis.deploy_text_does_not_resolve_defense: P22 explicitly converts an exhausted alliance to its printed number of dice for Deploy. That procedure is stated inside the Deploy check; it does not specify the accounting of excess strength during the different p33 defense procedure.

candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.reading: All newly exhausted printed strength must count, and exact equality is mandatory.
candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.case_result: Defense2 != attack1, so region is lost.
candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.missing_authority: Explicitly mandatory full-strength counting for defense, with no ability to meet a smaller threat while wasting excess.

candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.reading: A single alliance can meet attack1 using1 strength while its remaining1 is wasted, or overstrength defense meets the threat.
candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.case_result: Defense succeeds and no residual alliance strength remains usable.
candidate_readings_not_adopted_as_ruling.missing_authority: Explicit ability to waste excess/overshoot, or official clarification that meeting/exceeding attack strength satisfies p33 equality wording.

defense_analysis.importance: Survival versus Region Loss changes Commander removal/trophy loss, officer rout, Governor loss, control/loot state and escalating Company Standing loss. This is an essential procedural outcome, not cosmetic wording.
defense_analysis.novelty: Multistrength indivisible resource versus a smaller attack interacts with exact-equality wording. Existing equal-or-insufficient examples do not resolve this branch; it is not merely a changed numerical example under an already settled comparison.
defense_analysis.search_evidence_limit: Source-only researcher reports 912 forum titles indexed and38 relevant threads read, with no verified exact-case ruling. This reviewer checked the quoted primary passages and supplied source conclusions, but did not independently rerun that entire search. Absence of a located ruling is not proof that no ruling exists.
defense_analysis.handbook_and_current_text: The quoted Crown handbook says choose pieces to meet the Crisis and the reported current publisher-branded rules retain exact equality. Neither supplies the missing excess-alliance accounting rule; Crown text also lies outside the multiplayer scope.

fraud_correction.exact_ruling: At start of Revenue, roll one die per your officeholder. Remove min(current Company Balance, twice highest die) from Balance, and take exactly that removed amount from the bank. Balance£10/highest6 results in Balance£0/payout£10, not£12.
primary_derivation: Original article40838655 explicitly defines option2 as reducing Balance£10 to0 and paying player£10 when highest die6 doubles to12.
Cole Wehrle, author11406, article40850873, 2022-09-24, replies "#2 is correct. I'll see about clarifying the card."

The contemporary corrected card fixes timing to start of Revenue and Balance floor to zero; the designer reply resolves "that much" as actual Balance removed rather than uncapped doubled roll. No source here reverses that ruling.
fraud_correction.scope: Approve payout clarification and retained other Q078 corrections; do not revive superseded first-print "anytime before expenses" timing from the original question.
